title: First Response Communication Architecture: runbook & templates (draft)
body:
Purpose:
This is a compact, practical first-response communications architecture for SRE on-call and bridge leads. It prioritizes clarity, speed, and minimize customer confusion. This is a working draft intended to replace ad-hoc messages and speed up initial external and internal alignment.

Scope:
- Covers earliest 0-90 minutes of an incident: detection, acknowledgement, initial customer status page entry, templated email/slack customer replies, internal war-room checklist, and immediate follow-up actions.
- Not a full postmortem template; that lives under postmortems/ (link in linked_artifacts).

Key principles (short):
- One voice per channel: designate a Bridge Lead for internal comms and a PM/CS contact for customer comms if available.
- Rapidly declare a status page update within 5–10 minutes of confirmation.
- Keep external messages high-level; internal messages can include technical detail.
- Use plain language for customers; avoid speculation.
- Timebox updates: initial, 30m, 60m, then hourly until resolution or stable mitigation.

Incident severity -> communication posture:
- Sev 1 (customer-impacting: platform-wide outage): immediate status page + public slack alert + customer email to top-20 affected (if known).
- Sev 2 (degraded but partial): status page "degraded performance" entry + targeted emails.
- Sev 3 (minor/limited): internal investigation, optional status page if increasing scope.

Roles & responsibilities (quick):
- Bridge Lead: runs war-room, coordinates updates, approves external text.
- Comms Lead (SRE or PM): crafts status page and customer-facing copy.
- Engineering Lead: triage & root-cause path.
- Support Liaison: surfaces high-priority customers, escalates legal/enterprise tickets.
- Incident Scribe: records timeline and actions in ticket/JIRA.

War-room quick checklist (first 15 minutes):
1) Confirm detection: summary of signals (alerts, customer reports, telemetry).
2) Assign Bridge Lead and Scribe.
3) Determine preliminary severity and impacted surface.
4) Create incident JIRA/bridge link and pin in channel.
5) Publish initial internal Slack bridge message (see templates).
6) Publish initial status page entry (short + link to incident).
7) If customers affected, trigger email/SMS templates for targeted list.
8) Lock down who speaks externally (Comms Lead).
9) Start short-term mitigation (documented in ticket).
10) Schedule cadence for updates (30m, 60m, hourly).

Internal Slack templates (bridge channel):
- Initial (use within first 5–10m):
  [BRIDGE] Incident detected: [brief symptom: e.g., API 503s] affecting [scope: e.g., hosted-api production].
  Assigned: BridgeLead=@<name>, EngLead=@<name>, Scribe=@<name>.
  Severity: [S1|S2|S3].
  Incident link: <JIRA/bridge URL>.
  Immediate ask: Triage and confirm degr/impact + list top customer hits.

- 30m update (example):
  [BRIDGE U30] Summary: mitigation path in progress (e.g., rollback started / autoscale enabled).
  Impact: [reduced|stable|worse].
  Next steps: [eg, tracing, short-term patch].
  Needs: [eg, logs, quota increases, config toggles].
  ETA for next update: 60m.

External status page templates (short-form for public page):
- Initial public entry (critical):
  Title: Partial outage affecting text-generation and embeddings (hosted API).
  Summary: We are seeing elevated error rates and request timeouts impacting a subset of API customers. Our on-call team is investigating.
  Affected services: hosted API - text endpoints, embeddings.
  Scope: A subset of customers in region us-west1 may see errors or increased latency.
  Customer impact: Failed/slow API requests.
  ETA for next update: 30 minutes.
  Link: <incident page URL>

- Follow-up update (30m):
  Summary: Investigation identified a coordination issue in cache invalidation causing increased tail-latency. We have applied a mitigation (short-term cache bypass) which reduced errors for many customers. Work continues to stabilize.
  Customer guidance: No action required; some customers may see transient 500s during mitigation.

Customer email template (targeted, brief):
Subject: Service disruption update — Redwood hosted API
Hello <Customer Name>,
We’re currently investigating elevated error rates and delayed responses affecting the Redwood hosted API in us-west1.
Impact: You may experience failed requests or slow responses for text-generation/embeddings.
What we’re doing: Our on-call and engineering teams have identified a mitigation and are applying it now to reduce errors.
ETA for next update: 30 minutes.
Contact: Reply to this email or open ticket <JIRA link>. We’ll keep you updated.
Thanks for your patience — Asha Patel (on-call SRE)

Enterprise customer brief (if SLA/customer requires phone outreach):
- Call script (30s):
  Hi <Name>, this is <SRE/Support Rep> from Redwood. We’re investigating an issue impacting API requests in us-west1. We’ve applied mitigation and are monitoring; I’ll follow up in 30 minutes with a status. Are you seeing specific errors on your side?

Decision trees & quick rules (cheat sheet):
- If errors >= 5% of requests for >5 minutes and affecting >10 customers -> declare S1 and notify sales/CS.
- If only non-prod traffic affected -> internal update, no status page.
- If mitigation causes regression -> revert immediately and note in status page update.

Escalation matrix (names as examples):
- Minutes 0–10: Bridge Lead & Eng Lead.
- Minutes 10–30: Involve Platform Eng manager.
- Minutes 30–60: Involve Head of SRE + CTO (if S1).

Post initial period (30–90m):
- Move from reactive to diagnostic updates. Add timeline entries to incident ticket.
- Prepare customer-facing postmortem summary outline if S1/S2.
- Collect logs and retention snapshots; freeze config changes unless rollback approved.

Checklist for status page cadence (practical):
- 0–10m: initial public notice.
- 30m: progress update (mitigation/impact).
- 60m: status on ETA/resolution.
- Hourly: updates until resolved; final update marks incident resolved and links to follow-up.

Common pitfalls & how to avoid them:
- Overly technical external messaging -> keep customer copy to impact and guidance only.
- Multiple conflicting updates -> centralize through Comms Lead.
- No customer list -> maintain short list of top-20 accounts for rapid outreach (Support Liaison responsibility).
- Leaving updates open-ended -> always include ETA or next-update time.

Wrap-up template (final public entry):
Title: Issue resolved — hosted API (us-west1)
Summary: The incident impacting text-generation and embeddings in us-west1 has been resolved. The mitigation was applied at <time> and traffic has returned to normal.
Impact: Elevated error rates and latency from <time A> to <time B>.
Customer guidance: If you continue to see issues, please contact support with your request IDs.
Follow-up: We will publish a post-incident summary within 72 hours.

Post-incident quick postmortem starter (to capture in JIRA within 24h):
- Timeline of events (detection, mitigation, resolution).
- Root cause hypothesis and next steps.
- Customer impact matrix (regions, customers, duration).
- Action items with owners and due dates.

Notes & open questions (for this draft):
- Should we add an SMS fallback for top-tier customers? Pros: faster reach for outages. Cons: additional operational overhead.
- Automation idea: status page auto-creation from alert rule (include incident link).
- Add a short training checklist for on-call handoff (next doc).

Appendix: quick copy snippets (one-liners) for fast use:
- Internal one-liner: "Detected: increased 503 errors -> EngLead triaging; bridge open: <link>."
- External one-liner (status page): "We are investigating increased error rates for hosted API in us-west1; next update in 30 minutes."

End of draft.

If this looks reasonable, I propose a quick tabletop with Support and Product to validate customer templates and to finalize escalation names.
